elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: “HDI shall defend ... the Company and its affiliates against any third-party claim” subject to the enumerated covered triggers.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against covered third-party claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: “HDI shall ... indemnify the Company and its affiliates” for “all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees).”

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Coverage includes an allegation that “the Services or the Site infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Clause (b) covers “HDI's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include data breaches caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Clause (c) covers “any unauthorized access to or disclosure of the Company's data caused by HDI,” which operatively covers Vendor-caused data breaches.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Clause (d) expressly covers “HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of the claim.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must give “prompt written notice of the claim.”

elements.element: The indemnifying party must control the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim.”

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The clause requires the indemnified party to “provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.”

elements.element: Customer must indemnify Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: The Company must indemnify HDI for third-party claims arising out of “the Content provided by the Company.”

elements.element: Customer must indemnify Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The reciprocal indemnity expressly includes “the Company's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The only stated bases for the Company's indemnity are Company-provided Content and the Company's breach of applicable law; no additional Customer indemnity trigger is added.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: HDI must indemnify the Company against claims alleging that “the Services or the Site infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by Customer appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for compliance with Customer specifications appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP infringement remedies must include procuring the right for Customer to continue using the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no obligation to procure continued use rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP infringement remedies must include modifying the affected services or deliverables to make them non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP infringement remedies must include replacing the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing alternatives.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP infringement remedies must include a refund remedy.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No indemnity cap or three-times-annual-fees super-cap appears in the rendered clause.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position: bilateral third-party indemnities with the required Vendor triggers, protected Customer affiliates, and notice/control/cooperation procedures. The changes are confined to the requested indemnification framework and do not disturb the existing Globix provision. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its Customer-caused IP exclusions, infringement remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are omitted.
